concept.title: Generic Topic
concept.shortdesc: A Generic topic is the converter's fallback classification when the heading and body content together

conbody.p: A Generic topic is the converter's fallback classification when the heading and body content together do not provide sufficient signals to identify a Concept, Task, Reference, or Troubleshooting pattern. The most common triggers are a descriptive heading followed only by a <ul> list, mixed body content where no single element type is dominant, a heading verb and body structure that conflict, or a section with no introductory paragraph and no table or ordered list. A <ul> list on its own never triggers task classification — task classification requires both an imperative heading and an <ol> as the primary body content.

When Generic classification is assigned, the converter generates a standard <topic> element with <body>. All supported HTML elements are mapped in document order without applying the specialized structures associated with other topic types. When no introductory paragraph is present, the converter writes an empty <shortdesc> and flags it at WARNING severity in the conversion report. Generic topics are also flagged as candidates for manual reclassification if the content appears to match a more specific topic type.
